title: Attention lane-mask shared-slab aliasing causes transient mask application and KV eviction misalignment under speculative lane coalescing
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: After landing the lane-mask optimization (per-lane bitset compression + shared slab allocation) we began seeing intermittent token duplication, increased softmax variance, and KV slot eviction misalignment under high adaptive batching. Root cause appears to be mask aliasing when speculative lane coalescing merges lanes and the kernel hot-swap path reuses the shared mask slab without proper ownership semantics. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and a production-grade fix to eliminate correctness regressions introduced by the perf change.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Enable adaptive batcher with speculative lane coalescing (config: adaptive.batch_merge=true, batch.size_threshold=64).
2) Use model x-large-gpu-fp16 with input distribution heavy on short prompts and frequent prefill-decode interleaving.
3) Run continuous traffic at p95 latency targets to exercise hot-swap kernel selector (we used synthetic bench harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench/tree/attention-fuzz).
4) Observe occasional token duplication and rising softmax variance in 1-3% of requests; Datadog spike at the attached query pattern.
5) Repro more reliably by forcing kernel handoff between fused-attn and fallback-attn during mid-request by toggling kernel selector hint (see diagnostic harness in attachments).
investigation_notes: - Logs show that when speculative lane coalescing merges two lanes, the mask pointer is copied shallowly into the next kernel execution rather than deep-copied. When the runtime switches kernels mid-request the old slab can be reused by another request, causing a stale mask to be applied.

- Datadog trace correlation shows mask-mismatch events co-occur with KV eviction boundary misalignments; affected requests show a 1-2 token shift in KV slot indices leading to degraded softmax outputs.
- FP16 accumulation magnifies numerical drift; the same sequence in FP32 is less likely to fail but still shows mask inconsistency in correctness tests.
- Heap sanitizer in debug builds flagged unsynchronized writes to shared mask slab at kernel-hot-swap path (allocator ownership not transferred atomically).
- Reproduced locally using the bench harness with deterministic seed; attaching replay and core dumps in attachments.

- Hypothesis: optimization reduced allocations by pooling per-lane masks into a shared slab for perf, but missed an ownership transfer on speculative kernel merges; the allocator returned the slab to pool while another active stream still referenced it.
temporary_mitigation: - Rollback lane-mask slab pooling on runtime-1.20 canary clusters (config flag: runtime.flags.lane_mask_pool=false).
- Add a kernel-selector safety fence: when coalescing is active, pin mask slab to request until kernel completes (hotfix patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4621).
- Add a runtime metric 'mask_aliasing_count' and Datadog alert (threshold = 1/min for production) to detect regressions early.
- Disable speculative lane coalescing for affected customers via feature flag until fix is deployed.
- Ship a debug build variant with mask-sanity-checks enabled in a small canary (10% of traffic) to collect failing traces.
proposed_fix: 1) Change allocator semantics: allocate per-request mask pages when speculative coalescing is enabled; maintain explicit ownership token and refcount during kernel transitions.
2) Update kernel-selector to perform an atomic handoff of mask ownership during hot-swap (use 64-bit atomics and a lightweight epoch).
3) Add unit tests and fuzz targets that simulate lane merges and kernel hot-swaps to prevent regressions.
4) Extend CI to run the attention fuzz harness under both FP16 and FP32 nightly to catch numerical drift tied to mask inconsistencies.
5) Post-deploy: run a 72h canary with traffic shaping and runbook checks before full rollout to production clusters.
6) Long-term: consider making lane-mask pooling opt-in and only enable when sequence lengths and batching distribution guarantee no kernel handoffs (add heuristic to optimizer).
